newsitem.title: LATVIA: RIGA SHIPYARD SEES ONE MILLION LATS PROFIT IN '97.
newsitem.headline: RIGA SHIPYARD SEES ONE MILLION LATS PROFIT IN '97.

text.p: Riga Shipyard said on Monday that it sees a one million lats profit for 1997.
"Riga Shipyard's 1997 after-tax profit will be close to one million lats, slightly higher than in 1996," Vasilii Melnik, the company's president, told a news conference.
It earlier reported a first-half net profit of 451,735 lats on turnover of 4.63 million lats versus 3.61 million.
The company's production costs have also increased as Western clients, accounting for 65 percent of its business, demanding higher standards.
"Our production costs came to 3.99 million lats from three million lats," Eriks Kazha, board chairman said. "Demands that we have to fulfill have grown."
Some 20 percent of repair work is generated by Baltic ship operators and another 20 percent by the Russian North-West Shipping Company, Melnik said.
"The latter (the Russian firm) is close to insolvency, but we have reached an agreement that we keep any ship of theirs as a security until the payment arrives," Melnik said.
"One of their ships is currently in our docks."
Some 95 percent of the yard's business are repairs. The building of fishing trawlers, announced in the spring, is in the project preparation phase.
"Evereything is going according to plan and we expect drawings and specifications (from the Norwegians) to reach us at the end of August, in September," Melnik said.
The company earlier said that the first ship, if completed succesfully, could generate further orders.
"We have already invested around one million dollars in metal cutting devices and other equipment," he added.
